Klemco CS — Team User Guide

An end-to-end guide to the Klemco Customer Service application on ERPNext v16: every module, how to move around the app, and how the documents connect to one another. Written for the whole team — no technical background needed.

Company used in examples: Klemco India  •  ERPNext v16

1. Introduction & how to navigate

Klemco CS is a Customer Service and order-execution layer built on top of ERPNext v16. It adds a complaints desk, order-control rules (discount approvals, credit holds, automatic GST), a make-to-order flow for the Klemco plant, and dispatch tracking — all woven into the standard ERPNext selling and stock screens. This guide walks through each module, who uses it, and how one document feeds the next.

The two workspaces you'll use

A workspace is a home page with a left sidebar of shortcuts. You switch workspaces from the switcher at the very top-left of the screen.

  • Customer Service (Klemco CS) — your main home. It groups everything the CS team touches: complaints, order execution, Plant orders and configuration.
  • Selling (and the related Stock and Invoicing areas) — the standard ERPNext screens for Quotations, Sales Orders, Delivery Notes and Sales Invoices. Klemco CS adds its custom fields and rules onto these.

The sidebar groups

GroupWhat's insideUsed for
ComplaintsAll Complaints, Open Complaints, Escalated, Category MappingLogging and tracking customer complaints.
Order ExecutionAll Sales Orders, New Sales Order, Delivery Notes, Sales InvoicesTurning an order into a dispatch and an invoice.
Plant OrdersAll Plant Orders, New Plant OrderOrders that go through the Klemco (KM) plant.
ConfigurationDiscount Matrix, Category Mapping, client rulesSet-up screens, usually managed by supervisors/admins.

Finding anything fast — Search (Ctrl+K)

Press Ctrl+K (shown as “Search” at the top of the sidebar) to jump to any document, list or report by name. Type a customer, an order number (for example SAL-ORD-2026-00006), or a screen name and press Enter. This is the quickest way to move around without hunting through menus.

The tabs on a document

Every document opens with a row of tabs under its title. They organise a long form into readable pages:

  • Details — the main data: customer, items grid, quantities, rates, taxes and totals.
  • Address & Contact — billing/shipping addresses and the contact person.
  • Terms — payment terms and any terms & conditions.
  • More Info — extra sections, including the Klemco CS additions (Customer Service, Discount Approval, Credit Control, Dispatch & Tracking, etc.).
  • Connections — a map of every related document created from this one (covered in the next section).

2. The document flow & dependencies

This is the single most important idea in the system. Selling documents are created from one another, in a fixed order. You do not fill each one in from scratch — you build the next document out of the previous one, and the details (customer, items, quantities, rates) carry forward automatically.

Quotation→ Sales Order→ Delivery Note→ Sales Invoice→ Payment
The golden rule: you can only build the next document from a submitted (confirmed) one. A saved-but-draft document is not yet “real” and cannot be pulled forward. So the sequence is always: create → Save → Submit → then use the Create button to make the next document.
  • Quotation — the price offer to the customer. Optional, but the usual starting point.
  • Sales Order (SO) — the confirmed order. This is the anchor of the whole flow. It must pass the discount and credit checks before it can be submitted.
  • Delivery Note (DN) — created from a submitted SO; records what physically shipped and its dispatch/tracking details.
  • Sales Invoice — created from the SO (the system is configured so that an invoice must come from a Sales Order — you cannot raise a stand-alone invoice).
  • Payment — recorded against the invoice.

Tracing the chain: the Connections tab

Open any document and click Connections to see every related document, grouped by area (Fulfillment, Reference, Payment, and so on). The numbers tell you what has already been created. This is how you answer questions like “has this order been delivered?” or “which invoice covers this order?”.

Tip: The Create button (top-right of a submitted document) is the safe way to move forward — it pre-fills the next document for you. The Connections tab is the safe way to look back and see what already exists.

3. Complaints (CS Complaint)

Who: CS Executive, CS Supervisor, CS Manager

The complaints desk is where every customer issue is logged, routed to the right owner, tracked against an SLA clock, and closed with a resolution.

Logging a complaint

  1. From the workspace, click New Complaint (or the sidebar → Complaints → New Complaint).
  2. Choose the Complaint Type. The choices are Product — Quality / Damage, Product — Short Delivery, Non-Product — Delivery Delay, Non-Product — Billing / Invoice and Non-Product — Service.
  3. Set the Priority (Low / Medium / High / Critical). This drives the SLA clock — see the table below.
  4. Pick the Customer, and optionally link a Sales Order or Sales Invoice under “Linked Order” (a complaint can be logged even before you know the order).
  5. Write the Description, then check the routing suggestion and Save.

Auto-routing & assignment (how a ToDo is created)

When you pick a complaint type, the system suggests the responsible department and computes an SLA deadline automatically. The routing built into the app is:

Complaint TypeSuggested ownerSLA by priority
Product — Quality / DamageQC HeadCritical = 24h  |  High = 48h  |  Medium = 48h  |  Low = 72h
Product — Short DeliverySupply Chain Lead
Non-Product — Delivery DelaySupply Chain Lead
Non-Product — Billing / InvoiceFinance Lead
Non-Product — ServiceCS Manager

When you set the Assigned To user and save, the complaint is mirrored into that person's native “Assigned to Me” list as a ToDo — that is the notification the owner sees. Re-assigning moves the ToDo to the new owner.

Escalation, resolution & the workflow

Complaints move through a defined workflow using the buttons at the top of the form (they change with the current status):

  • CS Executive Start Review → Await Customer / Arrange Pickup / Send Resolution → Close Complaint.
  • CS Manager can Escalate an open or under-review complaint, De-escalate, or Reopen a closed one.
  • If a complaint runs past ~80% of its SLA it is flagged Escalated and the CS Manager is notified.
  • For product returns, tick Reverse Pickup Required to reveal the Pickup Docket field; on closure a customer-satisfaction (CSAT) survey flag is set.
Attachments & sharing: use the right-hand sidebar on any complaint to add Attachments (photos of damage, emails), Assign extra people, add Tags, or Share the record with a specific colleague (see §11).

4. Sales Orders

Who: CS / Sales Executive (creates); Sales Head & Finance (approve)

The Sales Order (SO) is the heart of the order-execution flow. Klemco CS adds three automatic controls to it — automatic GST, a discount-approval gate, and a credit hold — that must be satisfied before the order can be submitted.

Creating a Sales Order

  1. Sidebar → Order Execution → New Sales Order (or use the Create button on a submitted Quotation to carry everything forward).
  2. Confirm the Company (use Klemco India for GST examples) and pick the Customer and Delivery Date.
  3. In the Items grid add each line: Item Code, per-line Delivery Date, Quantity, UOM (unit of measure) and Rate. Any per-line Discount % is checked against the Discount Matrix.
  4. Save the draft. The system now runs its checks (GST, discount, credit).
  5. Clear any approvals/holds, then Submit.

The More Info tab — Klemco CS controls

The Klemco additions live on the More Info tab, grouped into sections:

  • Customer Service — Order Type: One-Shot (a single delivery) or Open (phased / staggered deliveries with a delivery plan).
  • Order Execution — Delivery Instructions (special handling, time windows) and the Preferred 3PL Partner (Mahindra Logistics, DTDC Freight, Blue Dart, or Others). If you pick Others you must specify the carrier.
  • Discount Approval — the Discount Approval Status and the Discount Threshold (%) that applies to this customer.
  • Credit Control — shows whether the order is on credit hold and why.
  • Client Order Confirmation / Mandate Documents — where the customer's written confirmation is captured.

Automatic GST — In-State vs Out-State

Klemco CS fills the Tax Category for you based on where the goods ship from versus where they ship to:

SituationTax CategoryTaxes applied
Dispatch (plant) state = delivery stateIn-StateCGST + SGST
Dispatch state ≠ delivery stateOut-StateIGST

The plant state comes from the company/plant address; the delivery state comes from the order's place-of-supply or the customer's shipping address. Once the category is set, the matching Sales Taxes and Charges Template is loaded and its tax lines are appended. You can still override this manually if needed.

Discount approval (the Discount Matrix gate)

Each customer type has a maximum discount % defined in the Discount Matrix (see §10). When you save a Sales Order:

  • If every line is within the cap, Discount Approval Status = Not Required and you can submit normally.
  • If any line exceeds the cap, the order still saves as a draft but is flagged Discount Approval — Sales Head. Submission is blocked.
  • A Sales Head / Sales Manager opens the order and clicks Approve Discount (or Reject Discount). Only these roles can decide; the approver is recorded.
  • Once approved, the block clears and the order can be Submitted. Bringing the discount back within the cap also clears the flag automatically.

Credit hold (the credit-limit gate)

On save, the system compares the customer's outstanding balance + this order's value against their credit limit:

  • If it exceeds the limit, the order is put On Hold with a reason, a red “Credit Hold” banner appears, and submission is blocked.
  • A Finance / Accounts Manager reviews and clicks Release Credit Hold. Only Finance can release it; the releaser is recorded.
  • After release the status becomes Clear and the order can proceed.
Remember: a Sales Invoice must be built from a Sales Order — the system is set so that “Sales Order Required” is Yes. No stand-alone invoices.
↑ Back to top

5. Klemco (KM) Orders

Who: CS Executive / Supervisor

A Plant Order (Plant Order) covers items that go through the Klemco manufacturing plant. It can be created two ways:

  • From a Sales Order — on the SO, use the Create → Plant Order button. It pulls the customer and each item, copying the SO quantity into SO Qty and KM Qty for the plant to review.
  • Standalone — open a New Plant Order and enter the customer and items directly (no parent SO).

When the plant is ready, submitting the order (“Confirm & Create Plant Order”) validates that every item exists and that any KM-managed item has passed its triple approval; the status then becomes KM Confirmed, and moves on through In Production → Inward Complete → Transfer Billing Done.

5.1 The Plant Order process flow

Every Plant Order moves through the same defined stages:

Draft→ KM Confirmed→ In Production→ Inward Complete→ Transfer Billing Done
  1. Raise the order (Draft) — create it from a Sales Order (Create → Plant Order, which pulls the customer and items and copies the ordered quantity into both SO Qty and KM Qty) or standalone (pick the customer and add items). Set the KM TAT Date — the plant’s target turnaround date.
  2. Review the quantities — on each line, SO Qty is the reference from the sales order and KM Qty is what the plant will actually make (defaults to the SO qty, editable). A Matches SO tick shows when they are equal; a banner warns if any line differs, so you confirm it is intentional.
  3. Confirm & Create Plant Order (Submit) — the system checks every item exists in the master and that any KM-managed item has passed its triple approval; the order then becomes KM Confirmed and goes to the plant.
  4. In Production — the plant is manufacturing the items.
  5. Inward Complete — the finished goods are produced and taken into stock.
  6. Transfer Billing Done — the internal transfer / billing between the plant and the selling company is complete; the order is finished. (Cancelling an order sets it to Cancelled.)
Who moves it along: the CS team raises and confirms the order (steps 1–3); the plant team then advances the status through In Production → Inward Complete → Transfer Billing Done as the work progresses. The system defines the stages; the team moves the order through them.
New item? Triple approval first. A new KM-managed item must be approved by all three — CS Supervisor, KM Plant Head and Supply Chain Lead — before it can be ordered. Until all three approve, confirming a Plant Order that contains that item is blocked.
↑ Back to top

6. Delivery Notes

Who: Warehouse / Dispatch team

A Delivery Note (DN) records the physical shipment. It is created from a submitted Sales Order — on the SO click Create → Delivery Note, and the items and quantities carry over.

Dispatch & Tracking

Klemco CS adds a Dispatch & Tracking section where the warehouse captures the shipment details. These three fields can be filled in after the DN is submitted, so the team can update them once the consignment actually goes out:

  • Docket / LR # — the transporter's docket or lorry-receipt number.
  • Tracking URL — a link to the courier's live tracking page.
  • Proof of Delivery (POD) — attach a photo, signature or GPS confirmation of delivery.
↑ Back to top

7. Sales Invoices

Who: Accounts / Finance

The Sales Invoice bills the customer. It is created from the Sales Order (Create → Sales Invoice on the submitted SO). Because the system requires an SO, you always start from the order, not a blank invoice.

Adding freight

Freight is not a separate custom field — add it as a normal charge line. In the Sales Taxes and Charges table, add a row of type “Freight and Forwarding Charges” and enter the amount. It is then included in the invoice total and the tax breakup.

COD cheque capture

For COD (cash-on-delivery) customers the invoice shows a COD Cheque Details section. The Is COD flag is set automatically from the customer type, and the Cheque No., Cheque Date and Cheque Amount (plus an optional cheque copy) must be filled in before the invoice can be submitted.

↑ Back to top

8. Quotation & Proforma Invoice

Who: Sales / CS Executive

A Quotation is the priced offer you send before the order is confirmed. It carries the same Items grid (with UOM), Order Type and tax handling as a Sales Order. Once the customer accepts, use Create → Sales Order to turn a submitted quotation into an order — nothing is re-typed.

Proforma Invoice: a Proforma is a non-tax, printable document generated from a Quotation or a Sales Order (via the Proforma Invoice print button, visible on a submitted Sales Order). It is used to give the customer a formal document to arrange payment or paperwork before the real tax invoice is raised. It does not post any accounting entries.
↑ Back to top

9. Payment Terms Template

Who: Finance / Admin

A Payment Terms Template defines when payment is due (for example, “30 days after invoice date”). Klemco CS simplifies this screen: the many advanced columns are hidden, a new row defaults to 100% Invoice Portion and a basis of “Day(s) after invoice date”, so in practice you only need to enter the Credit Days.

↑ Back to top

10. Configuration

Who: CS Supervisor / Manager, Sales Head, System Manager

Discount Matrix

The Discount Matrix is the master that drives the discount-approval gate on Sales Orders. Each row sets a Max Discount (%) for a Customer Type (and optionally a specific Item Group). If a Sales Order line exceeds the applicable cap, it is flagged for Sales Head approval.

Customer TypeMax DiscountMeaning
RC (Rate Contract)0%Rate-contract customers — discounts effectively blocked.
COD5%Cash-on-delivery customers.
Regular10%Standard customers.
All10%Fallback when no more specific rule matches.

A more specific rule (matching both the customer type and an item group) wins over a general one. Only Sales Head / CS Manager should edit these limits.

Category Mapping

Category Mapping (CS Complaint Category Map) is the reference table behind complaint routing: it maps each Complaint Type to an Assigned Department and an SLA (hours). It documents the routing rules the complaints desk follows and is edited only by the System Manager.

Client Scripts & rules

Much of the “magic” you see — the routing table on a complaint, the red credit-hold banner, the auto-GST, the simplified payment terms — comes from Klemco's client and server rules. These run automatically; there is nothing to switch on. They are maintained by your administrators and are listed under the app's configuration for reference.

↑ Back to top

11. Stock Management

Who: Warehouse / Stores team

Stock (also called inventory) is the record of what physical goods we hold, how many, and in which warehouse. Every time goods are received, moved, consumed, or shipped, ERPNext updates the stock figures automatically. The Stock module is where the warehouse team receives goods, moves them between stores, corrects counts after a physical stock-take, and checks what is on hand before promising a delivery.

Stock is the single source of truth for "what do we actually have?". Sales, Delivery Notes and Invoices all read from it. If the numbers here are wrong, deliveries and reports will be wrong too — so keep it accurate.

11.1 Warehouses & companies

Every quantity in stock belongs to a warehouse. Warehouses are arranged as a tree with two kinds of node:

  • Group warehouse — a folder that holds other warehouses (for example All Warehouses - KI). A group cannot hold stock itself; it only groups the ones below it.
  • Leaf warehouse — an actual location where stock lives (for example Finished Goods - KI or Stores - KI). Stock can only sit in a leaf.

Use company Klemco India (KI) for all real stock — it holds the GSTIN and is where our opening stock was loaded. Klemco India (Demo) (KID) is a demonstration company only; its SKU001–SKU010 items are sample data and should not be used for live work.

The Klemco India (KI) leaf warehouses and what each one is for:

WarehouseWhat it is for
Raw Material StoreIncoming raw materials waiting to be used in production.
StoresGeneral store / default holding location (the item default warehouse is Stores - KI).
Work In ProgressMaterials currently being consumed on the shop floor / part-made goods.
Finished GoodsCompleted products ready to sell and ship. Most Klemco (KL-*) stock lives here.
Goods In TransitStock that has left one location but not yet arrived at another (in-transfer).
Inspection HoldGoods held pending a quality check before they can be used or sold.
ScrapRejected / written-off material set aside from usable stock.
Amritsar Main StorePhysical store at the Amritsar location.
Thane Branch StorePhysical store at the Thane branch.

11.2 Checking what is in stock

The everyday "what do we have?" screen is the Stock Balance report. It shows on-hand quantity for each item in each warehouse, with values.

  1. Go to Stock → Reports → Stock Balance (or search "Stock Balance").
  2. Set Company = Klemco India. Optionally narrow by Item Group, a specific Item, or a Warehouse.
  3. Click Generate New Report to run it. Rows appear for each item × warehouse — for example the KL-* items in Finished Goods - KI.

What the main columns mean:

ColumnMeaning
Item / Item NameThe product code and its description.
WarehouseWhere this quantity is held (a leaf warehouse).
In Qty / Out QtyTotal received and total issued in the selected date range.
Balance QtyThe quantity on hand right now — the number you usually care about.
Valuation RateCost per unit used for stock value (FIFO).
Balance ValueBalance Qty × Valuation Rate — the money value of that stock.
Filter tips (shown on the report footer): in a numeric column filter you can type >5, <10 or =324 for comparisons, or a range like 5:10 to show values between 5 and 10. Handy for finding low-stock items quickly.

Other useful Stock reports:

  • Stock Ledger — every single movement (receipt, issue, transfer, delivery), newest first. Use it to answer "why did this number change?".
  • Stock Projected Qty — on-hand plus what is on order, minus what is reserved.
  • Reserved Stock — quantities already committed to orders.
  • Stock Ageing — how long stock has been sitting.
  • Warehouse Wise Stock Balance and Item Shortage Report — per-warehouse view and items that are short.

The Item form itself also has a "Stock Levels" dashboard showing that item's balance across warehouses.

11.3 Adding stock — Material Receipt

Use a Material Receipt Stock Entry to bring new stock into a warehouse when it does not come through a Purchase Receipt (for example a manual top-up, a found quantity, or loading a new item).

  1. Go to Stock → Stock Entry → New.
  2. Set Company = Klemco India.
  3. Set Stock Entry Type = Material Receipt. This reveals the Target Warehouse (where the goods land).
  4. In the items grid add each Item Code, the Qty, the target warehouse, and a Basic Rate (the receiving cost).
  5. Save, then Submit. On submit the stock is added and the Stock Ledger updates.

11.4 Moving stock — Material Transfer

Use a Material Transfer Stock Entry to move goods from one warehouse to another (for example from Stores - KI to Finished Goods - KI, or out to a branch store).

  1. Go to Stock → Stock Entry → New, Company = Klemco India.
  2. Set Stock Entry Type = Material Transfer. This shows both a Source Warehouse and a Target Warehouse.
  3. Add the items and quantities to move, set the source (where they come from) and target (where they go).
  4. Save and Submit. The quantity leaves the source and arrives in the target — the company total is unchanged.
For goods that are in transit between two locations, route them via the Goods In Transit - KI warehouse so they are still counted while on the road.

11.5 Issuing / consuming stock — Material Issue

Use a Material Issue Stock Entry to take stock out without selling it — scrapping, internal consumption, samples, or writing off a shortage found during a count.

  1. Go to Stock → Stock Entry → New, Company = Klemco India.
  2. Set Stock Entry Type = Material Issue (this shows a Source Warehouse only).
  3. Add the items and quantities, choose the source warehouse, Save and Submit. The stock is removed.
Selling goods is different. When you sell to a customer you do not use Material Issue — the Delivery Note reduces stock automatically when it is submitted. Material Issue is only for non-sales removals.

11.6 Correcting counts — Stock Reconciliation

When a physical stock-take disagrees with the system, use Stock Reconciliation (Stock → Tools → Stock Reconciliation) to set the actual counted quantity. Unlike a Material Receipt/Issue where you enter the change, here you enter the final number you counted and the system works out the difference.

  1. Open a new Stock Reconciliation, Company = Klemco India.
  2. Fetch the items/warehouses to correct, then type the actual counted Qty (and Valuation Rate if needed) for each.
  3. Save and Submit. The difference posts automatically to the Stock Adjustment account.

Stock Reconciliation is also the tool used to load opening balances for a new item or warehouse.

11.7 How stock ties to orders

Stock and Sales are linked end to end:

  1. On a Sales Order, "Set Source Warehouse" chooses where the goods will ship from.
  2. When the goods go out, a Delivery Note is raised against the order. On submit the Delivery Note reduces stock in that warehouse.
  3. Because negative stock is disabled, you can only ship what you actually hold.
Negative stock is turned OFF. If a Delivery Note is blocked because there is not enough stock, you cannot force it through. First receive stock (Material Receipt) or transfer it in (Material Transfer) to the shipping warehouse, then submit the Delivery Note.

11.8 Item settings that matter

Setting (on the Item)Why it matters
Maintain StockMust be ON for the item to be tracked in stock at all. If off, no stock is kept.
Default / Stock UOMThe unit stock is counted in (mostly "Nos"). Keep consistent.
Default WarehouseWhere the item defaults to — currently Stores - KI.
Valuation RateCost per unit for stock value.
Valuation MethodFIFO (first in, first out) — oldest cost is consumed first.

11.9 Serial / Batch tracking

The "Enable Serial / Batch Bundle" toggle only applies to items that are tracked by serial number or batch. Klemco items are not serial/batch tracked today, so leave this off — you can ignore serial/batch fields on stock entries and reports.

11.10 Klemco policies & gotchas

Use Klemco India (KI) for real stock and GST. KI holds the GSTIN and the real opening stock. Klemco India (Demo) is sample data only — do not record live stock there.
Valuation is a UAT placeholder. Item valuation is currently set equal to the selling price as a temporary measure. This must be replaced with real costs before go-live — until then margin/profit reports will read as (near) zero because cost equals price.
Current position: KI holds roughly 26,100 units across 52 Klemco (KL-*) items, mostly in Finished Goods - KI (e.g. KL-CA-001 = 300, KL-CA-002 = 800, most others 500), with zero negative balances. The demo SKU001–SKU010 stock sits in the Demo company.

11.11 "I want to…" cheat sheet

I want to…Do this
See what is in stockStock Balance report (Company = Klemco India, Generate New Report).
Add / receive stockStock Entry → Material Receipt.
Move stock between warehousesStock Entry → Material Transfer.
Consume / write off stock (not a sale)Stock Entry → Material Issue.
Fix a wrong count / load opening stockStock Reconciliation (enter the actual counted qty).
Know what is reserved / available to promiseReserved Stock and Stock Projected Qty reports.
Understand why a movement happenedStock Ledger report.
Know why I can't deliverCheck Stock Balance — negative stock is blocked, so receive/transfer stock into the shipping warehouse first.

11.12 Quick test: add stock → order → deliver → bill

A complete run-through to test the flow end to end. Each step is built from the submitted previous document using the Create button — never start from a blank Delivery Note or Invoice.

Step A — Add stock (skip if the item already has stock; e.g. KL-CA-001 already has 300 in Stores - KI):

  1. Stock → New Stock Entry.
  2. Stock Entry Type = Material Receipt.
  3. Target Warehouse = a real dispatch warehouse such as Stores - KI (not a Transit or Work-in-Progress warehouse).
  4. Add the item, the Qty, and a Basic Rate (the cost). It now auto-fills from the item’s cost; if it is ever blank, type a value or tick Allow Zero Valuation Rate on the row.
  5. Save → Submit.

Step B — Raise and bill the order:

  1. New Sales Order — Company Klemco India, pick the Customer, add the item and a Qty within stock → Save → Submit. Available stock is automatically reserved to the order.
  2. On the submitted order, Create → Delivery Note → Save → Submit — this ships the stock.
  3. On the order (or the Delivery Note), Create → Sales Invoice → Save → Submit — this is the bill; GST is applied.
  4. Optional: on the invoice, Create → Payment Entry to record the payment.
Tip: use the Connections tab on the Sales Order at any time to see the linked Delivery Note, Invoice and Payment — that is how you confirm where the order is in the chain.

12. Selling — the sales cycle

The Selling module turns an enquiry into a confirmed, delivered and billed order. Everything flows through a chain of documents — each one built from the previous, submitted one:

Quotation→ Sales Order→ Delivery Note→ Sales Invoice

A Sales Order can also branch to a Plant Order (production) — see chapter 5. This chapter is a map of the whole sell-side and the Klemco-specific controls built on top of ERPNext.

12.1 Where to find it

Everything lives in the Customer Service left sidebar, mostly under Order Creation and Approvals:

Sidebar linkOpens
New Sales OrderA blank Sales Order form
Open Sales OrderOrders not yet completed/closed
List of Sales order / Status Delivery Notes / Status Invoices"… — Created" reports (with Created On / Created By)
Proforma InvoiceSales Order list — raise a proforma from any order via its button
Quotations — CreatedAll quotations, newest first
Orders on Credit Hold · Pending for Discount ApprovalThe two approval worklists (under Approvals)

12.2 Quotation (incl. SITC / Project)

Quote a customer before an order. For engineering / SITC (Supply, Installation, Testing & Commissioning) work you do not key 30–40 BOQ lines — set Project Type = SITC / Project and you get:

  • Scope of Work — free text describing the job.
  • BOQ File — attach the bill of quantities (mandatory for SITC).
  • A single lump-sum line "SITC Works (as per BOQ)" is added automatically — just type the amount.

Click Proforma Invoice on a Quotation to print a non-tax proforma. Both the Project Type, Scope and BOQ carry forward when you create the Sales Order.

12.3 Sales Order — the heart of Selling

  1. Company = Klemco India (the GST company) and pick the Customer.
  2. Order Type — One-Shot (deliver once) or Open (Phased Delivery) (multiple deliveries; each line needs its own Delivery Date).
  3. Add items. Fast options: Import Items (upload a simple Item Code, Qty CSV) under the Get Items From menu, or type them in.
  4. Set a per-line Discount % right in the items grid (editable for Regular/COD customers).
  5. Attach paperwork — the Documents menu → Upload Documents lets you add several files at once (PO copy, test certificates …).
  6. Save, then Submit to confirm the order (stock is auto-reserved — see chapter 11).
Good to know: the Customer's PO shows as a column on the Sales Order list. Once an order has been billed, its item lines are locked (the "Update Items" button disappears). From a submitted order use Create for a Delivery Note / Sales Invoice / Plant Order — items pre-fill automatically.

12.4 Discounts & the approval gate

Each customer type has a maximum discount, set in the Discount Matrix (Configuration group). Edit these caps any time:

Customer typeMax discount before approval
RC (Rate Contract)0% (no discount)
Regular10%
COD5%
All (fallback)10%

If a line's discount is over the cap, the order is flagged Discount Approval — Sales Head on Save and cannot be submitted until approved. The salesperson sees an orange banner; a Sales Head / Sales Manager opens the order and clicks Approve Discount (or Reject) from the Discount menu.

Approvers are alerted by email + bell notification + a to-do, and every pending order is listed in the Pending for Discount Approval worklist. Sales Head Sales Manager can approve.

12.5 Credit control

If (a customer's outstanding + this order's value) exceeds their Credit Limit, the order goes On Hold on Save and can't be submitted until Finance releases it.

Accounts Manager opens the order and clicks Release Credit Hold. Held orders are alerted (email + bell + to-do) and listed in the Orders on Credit Hold worklist.

12.6 GST is applied automatically

You don't pick the tax manually. From the dispatch state (Punjab) vs the customer's delivery state, the order sets the Tax Category itself: same state → In-State (CGST + SGST); different state → Out-State (IGST). See chapter 13 for the accounting view.

12.7 Delivery Note

Built from a submitted Sales Order (Create → Delivery Note). Fill Dispatch & Tracking (Docket/LR #, Tracking URL, Proof of Delivery) and print the Delivery Challan (the default print). Stock is reduced on submit.

Stock guard: a Delivery Note is blocked at Save if the source warehouse doesn't have the stock — the message names other warehouses that do. Ship from a warehouse that holds the goods (real stock lives in Klemco India, e.g. Stores - KI). See chapter 11.

12.8 Reports & alerts at a glance

You want…Use
Orders still open (not completed)Open Sales Order
Who created what, and whenThe "… — Created" reports
Discounts waiting for approvalPending for Discount Approval
Orders stuck on creditOrders on Credit Hold

Whenever an order trips the discount or credit gate, the right approvers get an email, a bell notification and a to-do automatically.

13. Accounting — billing & payments

The Accounting module is the last leg: turning a delivered order into a tax invoice, collecting payment, and keeping GST and credit correct.

Sales Order→ Delivery Note→ Sales Invoice→ Payment Entry

13.1 Sales Invoice

The customer's bill (books revenue + receivable + GST). It prints in Klemco's Tally-style "Klemco Tax Invoice" format by default — Print on any submitted invoice:

  • GST is worked out per HSN/SAC — CGST + SGST for in-state, IGST for out-of-state — using India Compliance; amounts also print in words.
  • The e-Invoice (IRN / Ack No. / QR) block stays blank until government e-invoicing is switched on and your IRP credentials are added — a separate go-live step. The layout hides that block until then.
An invoice must come from a Sales Order — you can't bill a stock item that was never ordered. Freight and other services (non-stock items like Freight Charges / installation / SITC) are exempt and can be added straight onto the invoice, since they're added at billing time.

Two ways to bill:

  1. Normal: Sales Order → Delivery Note (stock moves) → Sales Invoice.
  2. Direct billing (no Delivery Note): tick Update Stock on the invoice → the Set Source Warehouse field appears → pick the warehouse; stock reduces at billing.
COD customers: a COD Cheque Details section captures the cheque no. / bank / date / amount / copy, and must be filled before the invoice is submitted. You can also raise a non-tax Proforma Invoice from the button on the invoice.

13.2 Payment Terms Template

Defines when an invoice is due. It's been simplified — you normally just enter Credit Days and the rest fills in (one 100% row, "Day(s) after invoice date"):

13.3 Receiving payment (Payment Entry)

  1. Open the submitted Sales Invoice.
  2. Create → Payment Entry — the customer, invoice reference and outstanding pre-fill.
  3. Enter the amount received and the mode (bank / cash / cheque) → Submit. The invoice's outstanding drops accordingly.

13.4 Credit control

Set a customer's Credit Limit (Customer → Credit Limits, per company). If a new order would push them over it, the order is put On Hold and Finance must release it before it can proceed — see 12.5.

13.5 GST — In-State vs Out-State

Klemco India is registered in Punjab (GSTIN 03AALCK8220C1ZX). The system chooses the tax automatically from where the goods go:

Delivery stateTax appliedExample
Same as PunjabIn-State — CGST + SGSTa Punjab customer → 9% + 9%
Any other stateOut-State — IGSTa Maharashtra customer → 18% IGST
Always bill on company "Klemco India" — it holds the GSTIN, so GST calculates and the tax invoice is complete. (The "Klemco India (Demo)" company has no GSTIN and is not for real invoicing.)

14. Cross-cutting: sharing, email & who did what

Sharing a document

Every document has a Share control in the right-hand sidebar (visible on the Connections tab, among others). Use it to grant a specific colleague read or write access to that single record — handy when a complaint or order needs another person's input without changing their overall role. Assign (next to Share) additionally puts the record on someone's to-do list.

Email automation

The system sends notifications automatically through the default outgoing email account — for example, when a complaint changes state (each workflow step can send an alert) or is escalated to the CS Manager. There is nothing to send by hand; as long as the default outgoing account is configured, the relevant people are emailed as documents move along.

Who created it, and when

Every document records its author and timestamps. On the Connections tab (or the sidebar of any record) you'll see “Created By” and “Last Edited by” with the time. In any list you can sort by Created On, and use the ⚙ (gear) → Pick Columns menu to add Created On and Created By columns so you can see, at a glance, who logged each complaint or raised each order and when.

Putting it together: log the complaint → quote the customer → confirm the Sales Order (clearing any discount/credit gate) → ship it on a Delivery Note with tracking → bill it on a Sales Invoice → record the payment. At every step the Connections tab shows you where you are in the chain.
↑ Back to top

15. Frequently asked questions

How do I see goods that are in transit to a particular plant?

Each plant has a dedicated “Goods In Transit” warehouse (e.g. Goods In Transit - KI). When stock is moved between plants with a Material Transfer, it sits in that transit warehouse until it is received. To view it, open the Stock Balance report (or the Item Stock & Open Orders report in the sidebar) and filter the Warehouse to Goods In Transit - <plant>; the Stock Ledger shows the movement history.

How do I know a Plant order’s goods are under production?

The Klemco (KM) Order status tracks it: Draft → KM Confirmed → In Production → Inward Complete → Transfer Billing Done. “Under production” means the Plant Order is at In Production; once made, it moves to Inward Complete (goods in stock). Reach the Plant Order from the Sales Order’s Connections tab, or from All Plant Orders in the sidebar.

Can I import a list of items and quantities from Excel into a Sales Order?

Yes. The Sales Order items grid has Download / Upload buttons:

  1. Click Download to get the template (CSV/XLSX).
  2. Fill in Item Code and Qty (and optionally Rate, Warehouse).
  3. Click Upload — the rows load into the grid.

Also handy: Add multiple (pick many items at once), and the full Data Import tool for large bulk loads.

Can I bill items from different plants using the same Sales Order?

Yes. One Sales Order can carry lines that ship from different warehouses/plants (each line has its own warehouse). From that single order you create multiple Delivery Notes (one per plant/warehouse) and multiple Sales Invoices — all linked back to the one Sales Order, which tracks delivered vs billed quantity per line.

One company at a time: a single Sales Order / Delivery Note / Invoice belongs to one company. This works across warehouses within the same company (Klemco India has Stores, Finished Goods, Amritsar, Thane, Work in Progress, …). If a “plant” is a separate legal company, it needs its own Sales Order.
